query.text: Lisette tonnage 1873 topsail schooner Duke of Sutherland decoy 1917
query.task_excerpt: How many tons was the topsail schooner "Lisette," built in 1873, which the Duke of Sutherland had formerly owned before she began working as a decoy craft in 1917?
query.claim: The trajectory's search result reported the tonnage of the Lisette as 76 tons and the final answer repeated 76 tons.

sources.title: Q-Ships and Their Story (E. Keble Chatterton, 1922), ch. VII "More Sailing Ships"
sources.excerpt: Even a private yacht was taken up for this work in June. This was the 116-ton topsail schooner Lisette, which had formerly belonged to the Duke of Sutherland. She had been built as far back as 1873 with a standing bowsprit and jibboom. She was taken from Cowes to Falmouth, where she was commissioned in August, and armed with three 6-pounders. But this old yacht was found to leak so much through her seams, and her construction was so light, that she was never a success, and was paid off in the following spring.
sources.applicable_context: Describes the private yacht taken up in June 1916 and the vessel the task names: 116-ton topsail schooner Lisette, formerly the Duke of Sutherland's, built 1873, taken from Cowes to Falmouth, decoy service through April 1917.

resolutions.reason: Applicability is decided by the task's own descriptors, not by repetition. The task names a vessel identified by four properties: topsail schooner, built 1873, formerly the Duke of Sutherland's, decoy craft from 1917. E1 states all four and therefore concerns the task's vessel; its 116 tons is the value the task asks for. E2 names the vessel and the build year only, identifies the photograph's creator, and cites no tonnage measure or register, so it cannot establish what the task asks.
